subject: general
question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Justice of High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** of a state is appointed by the **President of India**, as per Article 155 of the Constitution of India.
 
• The oath of office to the Governor is administered by the **Chief Justice of the High Court** of the respective state, as per Article 159 of the Constitution.
 
• While taking the oath, the Governor swears to preserve, protect, and defend the **Constitution and the law**, and to faithfully discharge the duties of their office.
 
• This procedure ensures the constitutional legitimacy and accountability of the Governor’s role in state administration.
 
• If the Chief Justice of the High Court is unavailable, the oath is administered by the **senior-most judge** of the High Court.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Appointment of Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the **President of India** under Article 155 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of **five years**, but the tenure can be terminated earlier by the President or by resignation.
 
• The Governor’s role is primarily ceremonial, but they also play a key role in ensuring the state government functions within the framework of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Oath of Office:**
 
 
• The oath emphasizes the Governor’s commitment to upholding the **Constitution and the rule of law**.
 
• It is administered in the presence of the **Chief Justice of the High Court** to signify the constitutional importance of the office.
 
• This procedure is designed to ensure a smooth transition of power and adherence to constitutional principles.
 
 
 
• **Responsibilities of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor acts as the **constitutional head** of the state, with all executive actions taken in their name.
 
• They appoint the Chief Minister and other ministers, summon and prorogue the state legislature, and can dissolve the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Governor has discretionary powers in certain situations, such as recommending President’s Rule under Article 356.
 
 
 
• **Relevant Constitutional Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 155:** Deals with the appointment of the Governor.
 
• **Article 159:** Specifies the oath or affirmation taken by the Governor.
 
• **Article 356:** Allows the Governor to recommend President’s Rule in case of constitutional failure in the state.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of High Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of the High Court is the highest judicial authority in the state and plays a vital role in administering the oath to the Governor.
 
• They ensure the constitutional compliance of this ceremonial procedure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Governor:**

 
 
• While the Governor is the constitutional head, the real power lies with the **Council of Ministers** headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• The Governor’s role is primarily to ensure constitutional governance and act as a link between the state and central governments.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Offices:**
 
 
• The oath-taking process for other offices, such as the **President of India**, is conducted by the Chief Justice of India.
 
• Similarly, the oath for **Members of Parliament** is administered by the President or their representative.
